report.summary: Chunk 4 of 6 of ledger.py: schema migration, pragma verification, transaction context manager, and write methods (record_intent, mark_completed, mark_failed).
risks: pragmas method | medium | Returns dict with keys from hardcoded list; if a pragma fails silently, the value is None; caller must handle None. | Check if callers handle None values.
record_intent | low | trace_id defaults to current_trace_id() but if that returns None, trace becomes 'None' string. | Verify current_trace_id() returns None or str.

_migrate | low | Raises SpineError if journal_mode not WAL; but pragmas() reads after migration, which may be after commit; if migration fails to set WAL, error is raised. | Ensure migration sets WAL mode before this check.

handoff.purpose: Schema migration, pragma verification, transaction context manager, and write methods for intents.

symbols.name: _add_missing_columns
symbols.note: Adds missing columns to intents table, specifically trace_id if not present.

symbols.name: _migrate
symbols.note: Runs schema migration: adds missing columns, executes schema statements, updates schema_version, and checks journal_mode is WAL.

symbols.name: pragmas
symbols.note: Returns dictionary of current pragma settings (journal_mode, synchronous, busy_timeout, foreign_keys) as reported by the database.

symbols.name: _txn
symbols.note: Context manager that begins an IMMEDIATE transaction, yields connection, commits on success, rolls back on exception.

symbols.name: record_intent
symbols.note: Inserts a new intent row and an event, returns an Intent object. Handles trace_id defaulting to current_trace_id().

symbols.name: mark_completed
symbols.note: Resolves an intent as completed with optional effect_id and result.

symbols.name: mark_failed
symbols.note: Resolves an intent as failed with error string.

claims.text: Nullable with no default: every pre-existing row becomes trace_id NULL, which is the truth about it -- it was written before any run had a correlation id.
claims.why: The code adds trace_id TEXT column via ALTER TABLE, which makes it nullable with no default, so existing rows get NULL.

claims.text: REPLACE, not INSERT OR IGNORE: a v1 file that has just been migrated in place still carries '1' here, and leaving it would make spine_meta lie about the schema the file now has.
claims.why: The code uses INSERT OR REPLACE INTO spine_meta, which will overwrite any existing row with key 'schema_version'.

claims.text: A ledger without WAL loses the durability posture this module is built on; that must be loud, not a quietly weaker guarantee.
claims.why: The code raises SpineError if journal_mode is not 'wal' (case-insensitive comparison).

claims.text: The durability settings AS THE DATABASE REPORTS THEM -- read back, not echoed from what we asked for. A pragma that silently failed to apply is exactly the failure worth surfacing.
claims.why: The method queries PRAGMA values directly from the database, not from a cache or previous set value.

claims.text: Every write runs here. BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock UP FRONT instead of on first write, so two writers never deadlock upgrading a read transaction (which returns SQLITE_BUSY without consulting the busy handler -- unlike BEGIN IMMEDIATE, which waits out busy_timeout).
claims.why: The code executes 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE' at start of context manager, which acquires write lock immediately.

claims.text: effect_key is the caller's after-the-fact identifier for the effect (see the module docstring). It is NOT unique-constrained: a retried intent legitimately reuses the key, and the ledger records both attempts rather than hiding one.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the schema definition of effect_key column; no UNIQUE constraint is visible in this chunk.

claims.text: trace_id defaults to the AMBIENT one (:func:`envelope.current_trace_id`), which is why converting this producer required editing no caller. The sole in-tree caller lives in spine/attempt.py; a run that opens envelope.trace_context() anywhere above it gets its intents correlated without that module knowing this feature exists. Outside a traced scope the value is NULL and the row is byte-for-byte what v1 wrote.
claims.why: The code calls current_trace_id() which is imported but not defined in this chunk; the claim about spine/attempt.py is external.

claims.text: payload is re-read from the canonical text, not echoed: what the caller gets back is what a later reader will get back (a tuple stored is a list read), so no code path is written against a shape that only exists in the writing process.
claims.why: The code returns Intent with payload=json.loads(payload_json), which re-parses the canonical JSON, ensuring consistent types.

claims.text: Close an open intent as COMPLETED. Rejects a second resolution.
claims.why: The method calls _resolve, which is not defined in this chunk; the rejection logic is not visible.

claims.text: Close an open intent as FAILED. Rejects a second resolution.
claims.why: Same as above; relies on _resolve not shown here.

observations.what: _add_missing_columns checks for trace_id only; other columns may be missing but not handled.
pragmas method returns a dict with hardcoded keys; if a pragma fails, the value is None, which might be unexpected.
record_intent converts trace_id to string if provided, else calls current_trace_id(); if that returns None, trace becomes 'None' string.
_migrate checks journal_mode after migration; but if migration fails to set WAL, the check may still pass if the mode was already WAL.
